title: terraform-module-stability-scenarios-and-rollback-cheatsheet
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working cheat-sheet and scenario playbook for module authors and platform engineers to use when making changes to terraform modules that power private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Focus: deciding semver bump, publishing to our internal registry, compatibility testing, and quick rollback/mitigation patterns.

Context / why this exists:
- We keep seeing small API changes in TF modules that cascade into long upgrade tickets for customers (state manipulations, provider pin mismatches, implicit resource renames).
- Need a compact, pragmatic set of steps and decision heuristics to reduce surprises and speed up safe rollouts.
- Companion to infra CI checks but intentionally lightweight so ppl can scan during PR review.

Quick decision matrix (author POV):
- change touches resource addresses (rename/remove/replace) => major bump (x.0.0), put in migration guide + warn in release notes + require canary rollout on dedicated pool before publish.
- change alters behaviour of default values or lifecycle/create-time behavior (e.g., changes to default network CIDR, resource retention) => minor bump (0.x.0), provide upgrade notes + compatibility tests, post-publish pin tests.
- purely docs/typo/metadata or non-runtime comments => patch bump (0.0.x) and normal publish.
- add optional argument with sensible default and no required change for callers => minor bump (0.x.0) if it could be used to change behaviour, else patch if strictly additive metadata.

Compatibility checklist (run before merging):
- tf fmt/check (GH action) ✅
- run module integration tests (module-smoke) against latest supported TF versions (0.13/0.14/1.0 etc as per module matrix) -> record results in PR comments
- run upgrade test: apply vN-1 -> import existing state -> apply vN and record diffs. If plan contains deletes or recreates, escalate.
- verify provider version pins; ensure provider upgrades are separated into distinct PRs where possible
- run consumer-sim test: pick 2 consumer repos that depend on the module (representative configs), run terraform plan/apply with the new module ref in a sandbox VPC
- confirm state addresses unchanged (grep state file for <module_address>). If resource renames unavoidable, add explicit state mv instructions and an automated migration script under scripts/migrations/vX_to_vY.sh

Registry publishing flow (internal registry):
1) pre-publish checklist: tag release branch with semver, update changelog.md with highlights and upgrade notes, add migration script if required
2) CI: must pass module-integration (smoke), upgrade-sim, security-scan (tfsec), license-check
3) dry-publish to staging registry: push module bundle to staging registry URL, run a full consumer-sim test using staging registry ref
4) if staging tests pass, publish to internal registry and annotate release in GitHub and Confluence (template in linked artifacts)
5) email digest + slack channel post: #private-deploy-updates with summary + expected impact + rollback plan (see below)

Rollback and mitigation patterns (fast actions):
- Safe rollback (no state changes): republish previous module version and advise consumers to pin to previous version; merge tiny revert PR to module to ensure registry has explicit previous release tag
- State-impacting regression: open emergency-migration ticket, create a hotfix module release that reintroduces previous resource address (if possible) or provide state mv script and run with customer permission. Escalate to SRE and success.
- Provider-induced incompatibility: pin provider in module to previous working range, release patch; communicate to consumers to NOT upgrade provider until migration window

Runbook snippets (copy-paste for ops):
- To run upgrade-sim locally (dev machine):
  1) git checkout release/v2.3.0
  2) terraform init -upgrade=false && terraform plan -out=plan.old
  3) git checkout release/v2.4.0 && terraform init -upgrade=false && terraform plan -out=plan.new
  4) terraform show -json plan.old > old.json; terraform show -json plan.new > new.json; diff old.json new.json | grep -E "(-/\+|recreate|delete)"
- If you see unexpected deletes: stop. Put PR back to draft and notify module-owner + QA.

Automated CI guards (recommended):
- integ-tests: matrix across TF versions we claim to support; fail PR if new tests fail
- upgrade-sim job: automatically attempt vN-1 -> vN upgrade; fail on any delete/recreate that affects resources tagged with lifecycle-critical=true
- schema-lint: enforce that all public variables have description + example
- migration-checker: detect renames by diffing module output names/addresses between tags

Communication templates (short):
- Slack: "Heads-up: published module X v2.4.0 — minor change (add optional arg). Consumers unlikely to need action. See changelog: <link>. Contact @<owner> if you see issues."
- Email for breaking: short subject "[ACTION REQUIRED] Module X v3.0.0 breaking change" with bulleted steps: pin, migration script, contact, ETA for coordinated rollout

Unresolved questions / TODOs (open):
- How long should deprecation window be for removed outputs/vars? 90 days? 6 months? Need legal/enterprise input for regen cycles with customer-managed private infra. (JIRA: INF-2345)
- Should we automate state mv in our private console for customers who opt in? Risky; needs SRE playbook + opt-in governance.
- Decide canonical list of consumer repos for automated consumer-sim (who picks them?)

Examples / small case studies from recent incidents:
- Incident: module network v1.7 -> v1.8 changed default subnet naming -> caused consumer config to lose references to security group attachments. Root cause: default changed w/out clear upgrade note. Mitigation: published v1.8.1 restoring previous default and added explicit variable for naming.
- Good: module storage v2.0 added an optional lifecycle create_before_destroy flag—published as minor, included upgrade sim and consumer tests, no incidents.

Appendix: quick semver guide (tf modules):
- MAJOR (x.0.0): breaking changes that require state manipulation or consumer config changes (rename/remove resource addresses, remove required variable, change meaning of variable)
- MINOR (0.x.0): new features, additive args, non-breaking behavioural changes with safe defaults (BUT still run upgrade-sim)
- PATCH (0.0.x): docs, metadata, minor bugfixes w/o state change

Notes to self:
- Move migration scripts under /scripts/migrations and build small runner to apply to an SRE sandbox project for validated runs.
- Add a quick checklist GitHub action that comments the PR with required test links (consumer-sim, upgrade-sim) when it detects diff in module API.

Contact / owners:
- module author rotation: @maya (owner) / Diego Rios (backup)
- registry ops: @nina

---
Draft status: lightweight reference for reviewers and module authors. Please add edge cases or local tricks you use in PR comments.
